artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $k$ and $n$, let $D(k,n)$ denote the minimum, over all choices of $k$ fixed points $q_1,\dots,q_k \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and all sets $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $|P|=n$, of the number of distinct values in the multiset
$$\{\, \|q_i - p\| : 1 \le i \le k,\ p \in P\,\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic order of $D(3,n)$ under the additional restriction that the three fixed points $q_1, q_2, q_3$ are not collinear. Equivalently, find matching lower and upper bounds (up to constants and polylogarithmic factors) for the minimum number of distinct distances between $n$ points in the plane and three fixed noncollinear points, as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known lower bound is $\Omega(n^{6/11})$ due to Sharir and Solymosi (improving an earlier $\Omega(n^{0.502})$ bound of Elekes–Szabó), while the only known upper bound in the noncollinear case is the trivial $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ inherited from the Guth–Katz distinct distances bound. No matching asymptotic has been established, so the problem remains open.
